text:
Mia Chen: Hey infra crew — opened PR #482 that refactors our terraform modules and pins provider/module versions. I also regenerated .terraform.lock.hcl and committed it. Can folks sanity-check for upgrade/compatibility issues before I merge? Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482

Sam Patel: Quick skim — looks sensible. Main ask: run a full plan in staging after doing `terraform init -reconfigure -upgrade`. Confirm no unexpected resource diffs. Also yes, commit the .terraform.lock.hcl (we should pin lockfile in mono-repo).

Priya Rao: A couple things to watch: did you change any provider source addresses? If we moved addresses (e.g. different prefix) we may need `terraform state replace-provider`. If not, `init -upgrade` + plan should be sufficient.

Mia Chen: No source address rename, just switched module sources from our internal git modules to registry modules where available and added version constraints. Providers I set to explicit constraints (example: `required_providers { aws = { version = "~> 4.60" } }`).

Daniel K: Heads-up: we have an aliased provider for the us-west account used by node pools. Make sure the modules accept an external provider or provider meta `for_each` if you changed provider blocks. Otherwise plan will try to replace resources.

Alex Kim: For pinning semantics: `~> 4.60` will allow bugfix/minor updates (4.60.x -> 4.61 etc) but block major bumps. That's sane. For terraform core constraint, set `>= 1.3.0, < 2.0` in root to avoid unexpected behaviour across CI images.

Priya Rao: Also run `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64` in CI to generate stable lock entries for our builder images. That helped us last time with flakiness when provider binaries changed.

Jen Morales: Security note — provider changes can affect import/replace behavior for KMS/CE resources. Please run the staging plan and then a targeted `apply -target` in a sandbox before wider rollout. Also check IAM drift alerts after the apply.

terraform-bot: CI: terraform fmt ✅, terraform validate ✅, plan (staging) pending — triggered by @Mia Chen.

Sam Patel: One more: if any module source versions changed significantly, consider a canary apply (dedicated-low) and watch metrics (latency/error) for a day. We had an issue last year where provider upgrade changed default lifecycle replacement behavior.

Mia Chen: Thanks all — I'll run the staging plan now and post the plan output here. Assigning review to @Sam and @Priya. If plan looks clean I'll do a canary apply to dedicated-low tonight. :thumbsup:

Daniel K: ping me if you want me to run the `state replace-provider` dry-run or help with aliased providers.

Mia Chen: Will do — will drop the plan link in ~30m.
